text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore High Court appoints receiver over assets of Workers' Party politician Tang Liang Hong, who faces various defamation suits brought by leaders of ruling People's Action Party.
- Woman whose gallstone removal surgery went wrong and led to her needing a liver transplant sues hospital and doctor, but settles for more than Singapore $1.25 million and costs.
- Deteriorating health of Chinese patriarch Deng Xiaoping forces Communist Party of China chief Jiang Zemin and other leaders to cut short provincial trips to return to Beijing.
- North Korea hints it could accept defection of top ideologue Hwang Jang Yop to South.
- Almost three-quarters of Singapore's closely watched listed companies expected to report earnings growth for financial year 1996 but numbers will probably be uninspiring.
- Former Sumitomo copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka pleads quilty to fraud and forgery at start of trial.
- Malaysian broking industry puts brave face on report investors may soon be able to buy and sell shares over automated teller machines and the Internet.
- Growing concern in Bangkok over danger of massive losses from forced margin sales as poor fourth quarter earnings reports drag Thai stock market further into doldrums.
- Large residential plot which could fetch well over Singapore $200 million put up for sale in Newton area.
- Mercedes-Benz still Asia's best-selling luxury car but BMW catching up fast.
- Keppel Corp's Philippine arm in talks with several foreign shipbuilders, including companies from Britain, U.S. and France, to build vessels for country's navy.
- Listed steel mill NatSteel Ltd, with Filipino partners, to build second steel mill in Philippines.
- Electronics and plastics company Omni Industries to launch initial public offering of 40-50 million shares.
- SESDAQ-listed Super Coffeemix Manufacturering says Malaysian subsidiary Super Food Technology agrees to buy stake in canned drinks company.
